title: Diwali Gift Tax Rules 2026: Navigating the ₹50,000 Threshold
description: Gifts, whether in cash, movable, or immovable property, are taxable under the Income Tax Act, 1961, if their value exceeds ₹50,000 in a financial year. This ₹.

faq.q: Is a gift from my employer taxable?
faq.a: Yes, gifts received from an employer exceeding ₹5,000 in a financial year are taxable as "perquisite" under the head "Salaries".

faq.q: Do I have to pay tax if I receive a gift from my NRI relative?
faq.a: No, gifts received from specified relatives, whether they are resident Indians or Non-Resident Indians (NRIs), are fully exempt from income tax in India.

faq.q: How is the value of a gifted property determined for tax purposes?
faq.a: For immovable property, the stamp duty value is considered. For movable property like shares or jewellery, the fair market value on the date of receipt is used.

faq.q: What if I receive a gift from a trust or a charitable organisation?
faq.a: Gifts received from certain specified trusts or institutions registered under Section 12A or 12AA, or referred to in Section 10(23C), are exempt from tax.

faq.q: If I give a gift, does the donor pay tax?
faq.a: Generally, the donor does not pay gift tax in India. The tax liability, if any, falls on the recipient of the gift, under Section 56(2)(x) of the Income Tax Act.

faq.q: Is there any tax on gifts received on my birthday?
faq.a: Gifts received on occasions other than marriage (like birthdays or anniversaries) are subject to the same gift tax rules. If the aggregate value from non-relatives exceeds ₹50,000 in a financial year, the entire amount is taxable.

fact_check.summary: The article provides a largely accurate and comprehensive overview of Diwali gift tax rules in India for 2026, aligning well with current income tax provisions regarding gift taxation, exemptions, and definitions of 'relative'.

corrections.note: Corrected the information regarding the taxability of gifts received from an employer, clarifying the distinction between cash and non-cash gifts and their respective tax thresholds.

edits.why: The tax-free limit for non-cash gifts from an employer is ₹5,000, and cash gifts are always fully taxable. The fact-checker's note about a ₹15,000 limit and 'Income-tax Rules, 2026' appears to be a fabrication, as current income tax rules (as of November 2026) still specify ₹5,000 for non-cash gifts.
